newsitem.title: USA: Green groups condemn Norwegian whale hunt.
newsitem.headline: Green groups condemn Norwegian whale hunt.

text.p: Wildlife advocates on Friday urged President Bill Clinton to apply pressure on Norway to stop commercial whale hunting.

As the Norwegian whaling fleet set off on its annual hunt, the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) and Greenpeace urged Clinton to use diplomatic means or trade sanctions to force Norway to comply with an international ban on commercial whaling.
An administration spokesman said Norway's whaling activity was being reviewed, but he declined to comment on the prospect for trade sanctions.
"The United States is opposed to Norway's commercial whaling and we're monitoring the current situation closely," the official said.
Richard Mott, WWF vice president, in a statement said Clinton was "on record promising trade sanctions if Norway continues its open defiance of the global moratorium on commercial whaling."
"Failure by the United States to stop Norway's expanded hunt brings us another step closer to the return of large-scale commercial whaling," Mott said.
"Norway cannot simply choose to accept or reject international agreements as it sees fit," Gerry Leape, Greenpeace's fisheries campaigner, said.
The whaling fleet was seeking to kill 580 Minke whales, the quota set by the Norwegian government that is about one-third higher than last year's kill.

Norway resumed commercial hunting of Minke whales in 1993, defying a global moratorium imposed by the International Whaling Commission and prompting the Clinton administration to raise the threat of trade sanctions.
"Norway has completely ignored President Clinton's warning, and has annually escalated its violation of the whaling treaty," said Mott.
Japanese whalers this week also were hunting a lesser number of whales for "scientific" purposes, the wildlife advocates said.
"President Clinton should get personally involved. He should tell these countries to stop, and if they don't, he should use sanctions," Leape said.
Leape said Japan's hunt was "commercial whaling under another name because most of the meat ends up in markets. We don't believe you have to kill whales to study them."
Norway has proposed opening commercial trade in Minke whale meat with Japan, and the countries are seeking to ease international protections for several whale species.
